Part of the [Command line reference](../cli.md), which lists the options for every command.

Usage: `lakana grant [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...`

Manage grants.

## `lakana grant create`

Usage: `lakana grant create [OPTIONS]`

Grant a role or action on a securable to a principal or group.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--kind` | text | required | INSTANCE, ENVIRONMENT, NAMESPACE or TABLE. |
| `--principal` | text | none | Principal name. |
| `--group` | text | none | Group name. |
| `--role` | text | none | VIEWER, ANALYST, DATA_SCIENTIST, DATA_ENGINEER or ADMIN. |
| `--action` | text | none | A single action, e.g. READ_TABLE. |
| `--env` | text | none | Environment. |
| `--ns` | text | none | Namespace (dotted). |
| `--table` | text | none | Table name. |
| `--override-managed` | flag | off | Change access in a scope an access file manages anyway, in an emergency (needs ADMIN on the instance; audited; the next apply reverts it). |
| `--reason` | text | none | Why, 10-500 characters on one line (with --override-managed). |

## `lakana grant list`

Usage: `lakana grant list [OPTIONS]`

List active grants, newest first; without a filter, every grant.

Filters combine. `--principal` and `--group` list the grants made to them (not those a principal has through its groups: `lakana access explain` says that). `--action` lists the grants that give an action, by itself or through a role; `--role` those of exactly one role (not with `--action`). `--env`, with `--ns` and `--table`, lists the grants on exactly that object. `--kind INSTANCE` lists the grants on the whole instance, which apply to every environment, namespace and table; `--kind` with `--env` must name that object's kind. A long list prints a "More results" line with the command that shows the next page.

A grant gives a role or a single action, so one column, `access`, shows whichever it is; it never drops. The table names who each grant is for in `subject` (`user alice`, `service ci-bot`, `group analysts`); the API answers with the names, so listing costs one request. Only an answer without a name shows the id and a notice (a server older than this CLI, or a person or group deleted a moment ago). A column with nothing in it is left out. When the terminal is too narrow the table leaves out `kind`, `namespace`, `table` and `environment`, in that order, and folds a long `subject` onto more lines, so that the `id` that `grant revoke` needs always stays whole, and a line under the table shows the revoke command; `--output json` always has every field.

A grant of `MANAGE_GRANT`, `MANAGE_GROUP` or `MANAGE_TOKEN` as a single action has the marker `no effect` in a `note` column, which never drops (a narrow terminal leaves out `table` after the others, so that the `id` and the marker stay whole), and a line under the table explains it, followed by the command that revokes each such grant with its whole id (the first five; `--output json` has all of them and carries the full sentence). Revoke such a grant, and give the `ADMIN` role to whoever should keep the ability.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--principal` | text | none | Principal name. |
| `--group` | text | none | Group name. |
| `--action` | text | none | Only grants that give this action, e.g. READ_TABLE. |
| `--role` | text | none | Only grants of exactly this role, e.g. ANALYST. |
| `--env` | text | none | Environment. |
| `--ns` | text | none | Namespace (dotted). |
| `--table` | text | none | Table name. |
| `--kind` | text | none | Only grants on objects of this kind: INSTANCE (the whole instance), ENVIRONMENT, NAMESPACE or TABLE. |
| `--limit` | whole number, 1 to 200 | none | Most rows to list (default 100). |
| `--cursor` | text | none | Continue after the page that printed this cursor. |

## `lakana grant revoke`

Usage: `lakana grant revoke [OPTIONS] {grant_id}`

Revoke grant GRANT_ID.

Take the id from `grant list`, which keeps it in the table even on a narrow terminal.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GRANT_ID` | text | required |  |
| `--yes` | flag | off | Don't ask for confirmation. |
| `--override-managed` | flag | off | Change access in a scope an access file manages anyway, in an emergency (needs ADMIN on the instance; audited; the next apply reverts it). |
| `--reason` | text | none | Why, 10-500 characters on one line (with --override-managed). |
